# Pre-Implementation Quality Checklist: Board columns

**Purpose**: Unit-test the requirements in `spec.md` — and, where they are cross-referenced, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md` and `contracts/` — for completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability and coverage, before R9 is treated as implementation-ready. Weighted toward the areas most likely to go wrong in this slice rather than spread evenly across the feature.
**Created**: 2026-09-04
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope of this pass**: the four delete refusals and their precedence under concurrency; case-insensitive uniqueness at the database; admin-only authorization and server-side validation; the four `column_*` activity rows and the widened `CHECK`; drag-to-reorder over the existing fractional `sort_order`; `kind` fixity and `updateColumn`'s surface; the delete confirmation; `AGENTS.md`'s eight change gates; and the blast radius into R5- and R7-owned files.

## The four delete refusals and their precedence

- [ ] CHK001 Is each of the four refusals given a distinct, quotable reason rather than a paraphrase a reader must invent wording for? [Clarity, Spec FR-034–FR-037, FR-038]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the precedence order stated identically everywhere it appears, and is "chosen by precedence rather than by evaluation order" defined as a requirement on the computation and not only on the outcome? [Consistency, Spec FR-038, second Clarification, contracts/mutators.md *The fixed precedence*]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for a column to which three or four refusals apply at once, including which single reason is shown and that the answer is stable across renders? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases 1–2, SC-004]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the requirement that the *disabled control's* inline reason and the *mutator's* refusal come from the same selection function stated as a requirement, or only as a plan-level design choice? [Traceability, Spec FR-039 vs. plan.md Principle III row, data-model.md §4]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the boundary conditions of `last_canceled_kind` and `last_done_kind` specified for a project holding two columns of that kind, and for a project holding zero (a state no path can reach)? [Coverage, Spec US3 scenario 6, FR-036, FR-037]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the spec state what `deleteColumn` returns when the target column is absent *inside* the locked read, distinct from absent at the initial resolve? [Closed, contracts/mutators.md — `DeleteColumnState` carries `not_found` for a column absent inside the locked read, distinct from `notFound()` at the initial resolve, and `MoveColumnState` now carries the same member for its two vanishings (Spec FR-010, sixth Clarification)]
- [ ] CHK007 Are requirements defined for whether a refusal is reported to a caller who bypassed a disabled control differently from one who never saw a control? [Coverage, Spec FR-040, US3 scenario 7]

## Concurrency, locking and the transactional boundary

- [ ] CHK008 Is the scope of the lock — the project's whole column set rather than the target row alone — stated as a requirement, with the reason it must be the whole set? [Clarity, Spec FR-050 vs. contracts/mutators.md step 1, research.md B-1]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the requirements for the moved-in-issue race expressed as an observable outcome a test can assert, rather than as a description of the mechanism that produces it? [Measurability, Spec Edge Case 3, SC-005]
- [ ] CHK010 Are requirements defined for the two-concurrent-deletes race for *each* of the three "last of" invariants, or only for the `done`-kind case the Edge Case names? [Coverage, Spec Edge Case 4, SC-003, FR-050]
- [ ] CHK011 Is a deterministic lock ordering required so two concurrent deletes on the same project cannot deadlock, and is that stated in the spec rather than only in the contract? [Closed, Spec FR-050 requires one fixed, total acquisition order over the project's column set, the same on every call and for both `moveColumn` and `deleteColumn`; contracts/mutators.md fixes the key as `ORDER BY id`, and T074 guards it]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "the response MUST carry the settled state" defined precisely enough to say what each of the four mutators returns on success? [Clarity, Spec FR-049 vs. contracts/mutators.md, where `updateColumn`, `moveColumn` and `deleteColumn` return a bare `{ ok: true }`]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for the client's rollback when an optimistic rename or reorder is refused — specifically what the user sees and where? [Completeness, Spec FR-027, FR-032]

## Name uniqueness, trimming and validation

- [ ] CHK014 Is the uniqueness rule stated as a database-enforced constraint with an explicit prohibition on a pre-flight read, in the spec and not only in the plan? [Clarity, Spec FR-004, FR-051]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for how the existing column's name is obtained for the inline error *after* the constraint violation aborts the write, given the transaction is no longer usable? [Gap, Spec FR-051, contracts/mutators.md "read afterwards, on the refusal path"]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the requirement that a violation of a *different* unique constraint must not be reported as a name collision stated anywhere in the spec? [Gap, research.md B-3 and contracts/mutators.md state it; spec.md does not]
- [ ] CHK017 Is case-folding defined for names outside ASCII, and is the spec's "folded to lower case" tied to a specific, deterministic folding rather than assumed? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-004, `OT-INV-016`]
- [ ] CHK018 Are normalization requirements beyond trimming — internal whitespace, Unicode normalization form, zero-width characters — either specified or explicitly excluded? [Gap, Spec FR-004, Edge Case 7]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the order of operations for a name — trim, then bound at 200, then compare for uniqueness — stated unambiguously, and is refusal (never truncation) required at each step? [Clarity, Spec FR-004, US1 scenarios 8–9]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the requirement that create and rename produce the *same* collision wording stated as a requirement on the message, or left to two independent implementations to match? [Consistency, Spec FR-021, FR-025]

## Authorization, the write boundary and server-side validation

- [ ] CHK021 Is the ordering "resolve the row, then check the role" stated as a requirement with its observable consequence (missing row reads as "This doesn't exist", never as a permission refusal)? [Clarity, Spec FR-010, Edge Case 11]
- [ ] CHK022 Does FR-008's prohibition on a client-supplied project identifier remain satisfiable given `createColumn`'s only project input is a client-supplied `projectKey`? [Closed, Spec FR-008 admits a project *key* as a lookup input resolved server-side and authorized after resolution, and bars only a client-supplied internal project identifier — which `createColumn({ projectKey, name })` does not take]
- [ ] CHK023 Are the requirements for the archived-project case carried by an acceptance scenario or a success criterion, or do they exist only as a Clarification and an Edge Case? [Closed, Spec SC-015 requires all four edits to succeed on an archived project on 100% of attempts with no mutator consulting `status`, carrying what the third Clarification, Edge Case 8 and FR-007 state]
- [ ] CHK024 Is "membership MUST NOT be a second condition" stated for reads as well as writes, with a criterion that can be verified against every query this feature adds? [Coverage, Spec FR-007, FR-009, SC-009]
- [ ] CHK025 Are origin assertion and actor resolution stated as requirements of this feature, or inherited silently from an earlier entry? [Traceability, contracts/mutators.md preamble steps 1–2; spec.md names neither]
- [ ] CHK026 Are the server-side validation obligations enumerated per mutator input — `columnId`, `targetColumnId`, `placement`, `name` — rather than stated once as a general rule? [Completeness, Spec FR-040, gate 3, Principle II]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the requirement that a refusal expose no SQL, constraint name, stack trace or configuration paired with a criterion that can be checked against each of the returned unions? [Measurability, Spec FR-052]

## Activity rows, the migration, and `column_renamed`'s `field`

- [ ] CHK028 Is the widened value list stated exhaustively — four values, named, and `column_recolored` explicitly excluded — in a single authoritative place? [Completeness, Spec FR-042, FR-005, Reconciliations]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for how this feature's `CHECK` widening composes with entry R8's widening of the same constraint, given both replace the same value list and the plan asserts they "may land in either order"? [Closed, Spec *Reconciliations* records that entry R8 landed **without** widening `activity_type_valid`, so this feature's migration is the only widening, takes the list from seven values to eleven, and has no second migration to compose with or order against (FR-042)]
- [ ] CHK030 Is `field`'s value specified per activity type, with `column_renamed` explicitly holding the OLD name and the resulting duplication with `from_value` named as intended rather than left to look like a defect? [Clarity, Spec FR-045, fifth Clarification, data-model.md §3 *Row shapes*]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the requirement that no activity row carries a reference to the column — so a row survives its column's deletion — stated as a schema-level requirement and matched by a verifiable criterion? [Measurability, Spec FR-045, FR-048, SC-012]
- [ ] CHK032 Are the requirements for `to_value` on `column_reordered` unambiguous about what `null` means, and is `from_value`'s deliberate emptiness recorded as an assumption rather than an omission? [Ambiguity, Spec FR-046, Assumptions — `from_value` on a reorder]
- [ ] CHK033 Is "written in the same transaction as the change it describes" paired with a criterion asserting the *absence* of a row after every refused write, verified against the database rather than through the feed? [Measurability, Spec FR-048, US5 scenario 5, SC-011]
- [ ] CHK034 Are requirements defined for a rename submitted with a value identical to the column's current name reaching the server — does it write a row, an `updated_at`, or nothing? [Closed, Spec FR-024 now states the server half — a submitted name equal to the column's current name returns success having written nothing: no change to the row, no `updated_at` touch and no activity row — so the outcome does not depend on which side noticed]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the requirement that column rows appear on the project's feed and on no issue's feed stated with a criterion that checks the issue feed, not only the project feed? [Coverage, Spec FR-044, US5 scenario 7]

## Drag-to-reorder over the existing fractional order

- [ ] CHK036 Is the one-activity-row-per-drag rule stated unambiguously — one row for the moved column, none for columns whose ordinal merely shifted — and distinguished from the collapsing rule that folds several drags into one line? [Clarity, Spec FR-047, first Clarification, US5 scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK037 Are the no-op-drop requirements complete: nothing written including `updated_at`, no activity row, and the same outcome for a bypassed call as for a UI drop? [Completeness, Spec FR-030, US2 scenario 3, contracts/mutators.md step 3]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the requirement that no ordinal, index or ordering key crosses the client boundary in either direction stated in the spec, or only in the contract and research? [Gap, Spec FR-029 is silent on the payload shape; contracts/mutators.md and research.md B-4 fix it]
- [ ] CHK039 Are the tie-break and ordering requirements for reading board order stated as a requirement rather than as an assumption a reviewer may accept or reject? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions — "row identifier as a deterministic tie-break", FR-033]
- [ ] CHK040 Is the keyboard-reachable reorder specified with criteria that can be verified without `@react-aria/test-utils`, which is not installed? [Measurability, Spec US2 scenario 4, SC-013, `AGENTS.md` → React Aria Components]
- [ ] CHK041 Are requirements defined for a drag abandoned, dropped outside the list, or dropped while another admin has concurrently moved or deleted the target column? [Closed for the concurrent-target case, Spec FR-010 and the sixth Clarification make both a vanished drag target and a vanished subject column `moveColumn`'s `not_found`, rendered as the stale-render case, with `invalid_target` reserved for a target that exists but is not a legal destination]

## `kind` fixity and `updateColumn`'s surface

- [ ] CHK042 Is the prohibition on `kind` reaching any mutator stated as a requirement on the *signature* — accepted by no call but the create, where it is a literal — rather than as a validation rule that rejects it? [Clarity, Spec FR-002, FR-003, FR-023]
- [ ] CHK043 Is `updateColumn`'s surface enumerated as an exhaustive exclusion list (no kind, no position, no project, no colour, not even as ignored optional fields) that a reviewer can check a signature against? [Measurability, Spec FR-023, plan.md Principle VI row]
- [ ] CHK044 Is the requirement that every column added after project creation carries `open` stated together with a criterion covering a project whose seeded columns have all been renamed or reordered? [Coverage, Spec FR-003, SC-008, Edge Case 13]

## The delete confirmation

- [ ] CHK045 Is the confirmation requirement specific about what "naming the column" means in the dialog, and is the once-only rule stated so a second confirmation cannot be added later without a spec change? [Clarity, Spec FR-039, fourth Clarification]
- [ ] CHK046 Are the dismiss, cancel and Escape paths specified as writing nothing, making no call, leaving the activity feed untouched, and returning focus — with each of those four consequences stated rather than implied? [Completeness, Spec FR-039, Edge Case 9, SC-014]
- [ ] CHK047 Is the "visible and disabled with an inline reason, never hidden and never dead" requirement for an admin's Delete reconciled explicitly against FR-016's read-only treatment for a non-admin? [Consistency, Spec FR-039 vs. FR-016, Reconciliations]

## `AGENTS.md`'s eight change gates

- [ ] CHK048 Is the Red step for the schema change specified concretely enough to be observed failing — an insert refused by the un-widened `CHECK`, not a type error? [Measurability, gate 1, Principle VII, plan.md Principle VII row, research.md F-3]
- [ ] CHK049 Are the requirements that must be proven against a real PostgreSQL instance — the two races, the four invariants, the uniqueness constraint — enumerated so no one of them is satisfied by a mock? [Completeness, gate 1/8, `AGENTS.md` → Testing, research.md F-1, F-2]
- [ ] CHK050 Is the zero-new-dependency position stated with the refused alternatives named, so a later reviewer meets the decision rather than rediscovering it? [Traceability, gate 4, Principle IV, plan.md Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK051 Are the three places a reader would want an explanatory comment identified, with the requirement that each is answered by naming or by the design documents rather than by an annotation? [Traceability, gate 6, Principles V and VI, plan.md Principle V row]
- [ ] CHK052 Does every path listed in the plan's Project Structure carry a requirement identifier, so gate 7's "every changed line traces to a requirement" is checkable from the plan alone? [Traceability, gate 7, plan.md Source code]

## Blast radius into R5- and R7-owned files

- [ ] CHK053 Are the three R7 edits — two `ActivityType` unions and `buildSentence`'s exhaustive switch — recorded as forced consequences with the failure that occurs if any is skipped? [Completeness, plan.md Complexity Tracking, research.md C-2]
- [ ] CHK054 Is the decision to widen rather than deduplicate R7's two independent `ActivityType` declarations stated explicitly, so a reviewer does not read the duplication as an oversight? [Clarity, data-model.md §4, gate 7]
- [ ] CHK055 Is `EditableField`'s fourth result variant specified with its full contract — inline, `role="alert"`, still rolling back, and unused by R5's existing callers? [Completeness, plan.md Complexity Tracking, contracts/screens.md]
- [ ] CHK056 Are the requirements for `ProjectColumnRow`'s two changed fields — a live `issueCount` replacing R5's hardcoded zero, and a new `deleteRefusal` — traced to the FRs that force each change? [Traceability, Spec FR-015, FR-039, data-model.md §4]
- [ ] CHK057 Is the change to R5's existing `columns-section` test specified as in-scope for this feature, with the assertion that must change and the one that survives named? [Completeness, plan.md *Not recorded as complexity*, FR-013, FR-014]

## Ambiguities, conflicts and assumptions

- [ ] CHK058 Does SC-010's claim that the shown count and the refusal's count "never disagree, so no enabled Delete control ever produces the 'still holds issues' refusal" conflict with Edge Case 3 and SC-005, which require exactly that refusal when an issue is moved in after the control was rendered? [Closed, Spec SC-010 now states that the control's enabled state describes the last render and is not a promise about the server, the emptiness refusal being re-evaluated inside the delete's own lock, which reconciles it with SC-005 and Edge Case 3]
- [ ] CHK059 Are the four "defaults chosen because the source is silent" each stated with the cost of being wrong, and is each one a candidate a reviewer can accept or reject independently? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK060 Are the three reconciliations against `requirements-index.md` — the fifth `column_recolored` type, the seven-value palette, and the "five events" count — resolved in one place a later reader will find before writing the migration? [Consistency, Spec Reconciliations, FR-042]
- [ ] CHK061 Is the obligation placed on R7's writing function — that it accept any value the `CHECK` admits at the time it runs — verified against the shipped function rather than assumed from R7's FR-011? [Assumption, Spec *Obligations this feature places on entries built before it*]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK006, CHK022, CHK034 and CHK058 each named a concrete inconsistency found while generating this list. All four have since been corrected in the artifacts themselves — `contracts/mutators.md` carries `not_found` on `DeleteColumnState` and on `MoveColumnState` (CHK006), and `spec.md`'s FR-008, FR-024 and SC-010 close the other three — and CHK011, CHK023, CHK029 and CHK041 likewise. Each of those items keeps its question, with its bracketed annotation rewritten to describe what now closes it; every one stays unticked, because a reviewer ticks these, never an agent
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
